slides.0.title: Niagara Peninsula Sub-Appellations
slides.0.subtitle: The sub-appellations, soils and styles of the Niagara Escarpment and Niagara-on-the-Lake
slides.1.title: Niagara's three regional appellations
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Niagara Escarpment
slides.1.highlights.0.content: The bench lands along the escarpment, from west of St. Catharines to Grimsby, with three sub-appellations: Short Hills Bench, Twenty Mile Bench and Beamsville Bench (VQA Ontario, Wine With Seth)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Niagara-on-the-Lake
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Four sub-appellations: Niagara Lakeshore, Four Mile Creek, St. David's Bench and Niagara River (Wine With Seth)
slides.1.highlights.2.title: West Niagara
slides.1.highlights.2.content: The remaining three sub-appellations are Lincoln Lakeshore, Creek Shores and Vinemount Ridge. VQA's West Niagara page also lists the three Escarpment benches for six in all, which does not match the total of 10, so this course uses the 3 + 4 + 3 split and does not test it (VQA Ontario, Wine With Seth)
slides.1.content: The 10 sub-appellations can be remembered as 3 + 4 + 3.
slides.2.title: The Escarpment's three benches
slides.2.highlights.0.title: East to west
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Short Hills Bench is easternmost, between Twelve Mile Creek and Fifteen Mile Creek; Twenty Mile Bench is in the middle, from Fifteen Mile Creek to just west of Cherry Avenue, with a double-bench formation; Beamsville Bench is westernmost, from the escarpment north to Regional Road 81, at the base of the Lake Iroquois Shore Bluff (VQA Ontario)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Soils and minerality
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Soils vary widely, from water-stratified clay and silt to rich calcareous clay loam; most are deep and moderately drained with good water-holding capacity. The underlying fossil-enriched sedimentary dolomites are linked to the minerality of many bench wines (VQA Ontario)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Common grapes
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Chardonnay, Riesling, Pinot Noir, Cabernet Franc and Gamay Noir (VQA Ontario)
slides.2.content: The benches turn on slope, soil and the escarpment's shelter.
slides.3.title: How the escarpment shapes climate
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Shelter and reflection
slides.3.highlights.0.content: The escarpment shelters vines from strong southwesterly winds and reflects lake breezes (VQA Ontario)
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Delayed bud-burst in spring
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Spring warms gradually, delaying bud-burst and reducing frost risk; in autumn the slopes trap warm lake air and extend the growing season (VQA Ontario)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Cooler nights higher up
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Cooler nights at higher elevations support ripening and balanced acidity (VQA Ontario); sources differ on escarpment height (a 60–100 m ridge, or about 177 m at most), so it is not tested
slides.3.content: The escarpment lets spring arrive later and autumn linger.
